answer.rationale: Expiration in 14 days is a formal renewal point, distinct from the mid-cycle reopen the incumbent already refused. Prior renewals moved price and terms via benchmarking, and multi-year commitments unlocked volume pricing without shrinking scope or destabilizing integration. That path can pursue the 18% spend cut while keeping the incumbent and therefore not raising delivery risk on a 94% no-buffer line. Switch or lapse would add migration/coverage risk the objective forbids; dual-source would not itself replace the expiring primary contract under a one-decision limit. Whether an 18% move is achievable remains uncertain pending the archived renegotiation record.
